settings.description: Auto-stash changes when switching
settings.detailedDescription: Automatically stash uncommitted changes when switching branches. When enabled, Kunj will save your work-in-progress before switching and restore it when you return to the branch. This prevents losing uncommitted changes when moving between branches.
examples: false - Never stash, require clean working tree

settings.description: Sort: recent/alphabetical
settings.detailedDescription: Determines how branches are sorted in lists and menus. "recent" sorts by last activity (most recently used first), while "alphabetical" sorts branches by name in A-Z order.
examples: recent - Show most recently used branches first

settings.description: Items per page
settings.detailedDescription: Number of items to display per page in interactive menus. Larger values show more items at once but may be harder to navigate. Smaller values require more scrolling but are easier to scan.

settings.description: Use Unicode in graph
settings.detailedDescription: Use Unicode box-drawing characters (│ ├ ─ ╮ ╯ ●) instead of ASCII (* | / \) in commit graphs. Unicode provides a more polished, continuous look but may not render correctly in all terminals.
examples: true - Use Unicode characters for prettier graphs
false - Use ASCII characters for compatibility (default)

settings.description: Graph color style
settings.detailedDescription: Color scheme for commit graphs. Choose based on your terminal background: "default" for balanced colors, "light" optimized for light backgrounds with darker colors, "dark" optimized for dark backgrounds with brighter colors.
examples: light - Optimized for light terminal backgrounds
dark - Optimized for dark terminal backgrounds

settings.description: Default base branch for new branches and PRs
settings.detailedDescription: The branch new branches are created from (kunj create, switch -c, worktree add -b/-c) and that pull requests target. Common values are "main", "master", or "develop". If not set, the repository default (origin/HEAD, else main or master) is used. --base overrides it for one command.
examples: main - Use main as the default base branch
master - Use master as the default base branch
develop - Use develop as the default base branch

settings.description: Create new branches from origin
settings.detailedDescription: Fetch the base branch from origin and create new branches from origin/<base> rather than the local copy, so they start from the latest remote commit. Falls back to the local branch when the repository has no origin or the branch is not on it. --no-origin turns it off for one command. New branches never track the base; push them with -u as usual.
examples: true - Fetch and branch from origin/<base> (default)
false - Branch from the local <base> without fetching

Filter to configured branches
Personal WIP detection
Days for recent branches
WIP tags
Done tags

Commit message style
settings.detailedDescription: Choose the format for AI-generated commit messages and PR descriptions. Each style follows different conventions for organizing and presenting changes. This applies to both commit messages and pull request descriptions.
examples: custom - Use customInstructions for your own format

settings.description: Max subject line length
Include detailed body
Custom AI instructions
settings.detailedDescription: Additional instructions for the AI to follow when generating commit messages and PR descriptions. Use this to enforce team conventions, add specific requirements, or customize the output format. These instructions are added to all AI prompts.
examples: "Focus on business value over technical details"

settings.description: Auto-generate PR descriptions
settings.detailedDescription: When enabled, AI automatically generates pull request titles and descriptions when you run "kunj pr". The AI analyzes code changes, commit history, and branch metadata to create comprehensive PR descriptions. Falls back to heuristic generation if AI fails.
examples: true - Use AI for PR descriptions (recommended)

settings.description: Include full diff for PR context
settings.detailedDescription: When generating PR descriptions, include the full code diff for AI analysis. This provides better context and more accurate descriptions, but may be slower for large changes. If disabled, the AI only uses commit messages and branch metadata.
examples: true - Analyze full code changes (better quality)

settings.description: Enable Git Flow
settings.detailedDescription: Enable Git Flow branching model in this repository. When enabled, you can use the `kunj flow` command to manage feature, release, and hotfix branches following the Git Flow methodology.

settings.description: Main/production branch
settings.detailedDescription: The main production branch where stable releases are maintained. This is typically "main" or "master". Release and hotfix branches will be merged into this branch.
examples: main - Use main as production branch (default)
master - Use master as production branch

settings.description: Development branch
settings.detailedDescription: The integration branch for ongoing development. Feature branches are created from and merged back into this branch. This is typically "develop" or "dev".
examples: develop - Use develop as integration branch (default)
dev - Use dev as integration branch
development - Use development as integration branch

settings.description: Feature branch prefix
settings.detailedDescription: Prefix for feature branch names. Feature branches are created for new features and improvements. Use empty string for no prefix.

settings.description: Release branch prefix
settings.detailedDescription: Prefix for release branch names. Release branches are created to prepare new production releases. Use empty string for no prefix.

settings.description: Hotfix branch prefix
settings.detailedDescription: Prefix for hotfix branch names. Hotfix branches are created from production to quickly patch critical bugs. Use empty string for no prefix.

settings.description: Auto-delete branch after finish
settings.detailedDescription: Automatically delete feature/release/hotfix branches after successfully finishing them. When disabled, you will be prompted to confirm deletion for each branch.
examples: true - Automatically delete branches after merge (default)
false - Always ask before deleting branches

settings.description: Git Flow mode: local or pr
settings.detailedDescription: Choose how Git Flow operations are performed. "local" uses local git merges, while "pr" creates and merges pull requests on your remote provider (GitHub, GitLab, etc.).
examples: pr - Use pull requests on remote provider

settings.description: PR provider: github or gitlab
settings.detailedDescription: The pull request provider to use when flow.mode is set to "pr". Currently supports GitHub and GitLab.

settings.description: Merge releases/hotfixes back to develop
settings.detailedDescription: After finishing a release or hotfix, automatically merge the changes back into the develop branch. This keeps develop up to date with production fixes and releases.
examples: true - Merge back to develop after release/hotfix (default)
false - Do not merge back to develop

settings.description: Jira integration enabled
settings.detailedDescription: Enable Jira Cloud integration for ticket management and automatic branch-ticket linking. When enabled, Kunj can list tickets, create issues, and automatically link branches to Jira tickets.

settings.description: Jira Cloud URL
settings.detailedDescription: Your Jira Cloud instance URL (e.g., https://company.atlassian.net). This is required for API access.

settings.description: Jira account email
settings.detailedDescription: Email address associated with your Jira account. Used for authentication with API token.

settings.description: Jira API token
settings.detailedDescription: API token for authentication. Generate at https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens

settings.description: Default project key
settings.detailedDescription: Default Jira project key to use when creating tickets (e.g., PROJ, DEV). You can override this when creating tickets.

settings.description: Default issue type
settings.detailedDescription: Default type when creating Jira tickets. Can be overridden with --type flag.

settings.description: Board ID for sprints
settings.detailedDescription: Jira board ID for sprint operations (optional). Used by "kunj jira list --sprint" to show tickets in active sprint. Find this in your board URL.

settings.description: Use AI to generate tickets
settings.detailedDescription: When enabled, AI will automatically analyze branch commits and generate ticket summaries and descriptions when creating Jira tickets. Requires AI to be enabled.

settings.description: Slack integration enabled
settings.detailedDescription: Enable Slack integration to pull channel activity into team reports. Requires a Slack app with channels:history, channels:read, groups:read, groups:history, and users:read scopes.

settings.description: Slack Bot OAuth token
settings.detailedDescription: Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-...) from your Slack app. Found under OAuth & Permissions in your app settings. Requires scopes: channels:history, channels:read, groups:read, groups:history, users:read.

settings.description: Slack signing secret
settings.detailedDescription: Signing Secret from your Slack app's Basic Information page. Used to verify requests originate from Slack.

settings.description: Slack App-Level token
settings.detailedDescription: App-Level Token (xapp-...) for Socket Mode. Generate under Basic Information → App-Level Tokens with connections:write scope. Optional — only needed for Socket Mode features.

settings.description: Channels to post reports to
settings.detailedDescription: Slack channel IDs to post team reports to. Reports are automatically posted to all listed channels when running "kunj team". Configure via interactive editor for a channel selector.

settings.description: Directory where new worktrees are created
settings.detailedDescription: Supports ${repoconfig} (the .git directory, or the repository itself when bare), ${repoRoot}, ${repoName}, ${home} and ${branch}. Relative paths are resolved from the main repository root. Unless ${branch} appears, the branch directory is appended automatically.

settings.description: Command used by `kunj worktree open` to open a worktree
settings.detailedDescription: The worktree path is appended as the last argument. For VS Code-style editors (code, cursor, codium, windsurf) kunj adds -r to reuse the current window, or -n with --new-window. Set to an empty string to disable opening an editor.
examples: code - Open in Visual Studio Code (default)
code -n - Always open a new VS Code window

settings.description: Directory `kunj repos clone` clones repositories into
settings.detailedDescription: The repository is cloned to <cloneDir>/<name> (<name>.git with repos.cloneBare). A leading ~ and ${home} are expanded; --dir overrides it for one clone.

settings.description: Clone as a bare repository with a worktree for the default branch
settings.detailedDescription: When true, `kunj repos clone` makes <cloneDir>/<name>.git bare, fetching origin into refs/remotes/origin, and adds a worktree for the default branch where worktree.baseDir puts it. --bare / --no-bare override it for one clone.

settings.description: Command run by the pre-worktree-create hook
settings.detailedDescription: Runs before `kunj worktree add` creates a worktree. A non-zero exit aborts the creation. The command runs through the shell with ${repoRoot}, ${repoconfig}, ${repoName}, ${home}, ${worktree}, ${worktreePath}, ${branch} expanded, and receives KUNJ_HOOK, KUNJ_REPO_ROOT, KUNJ_WORKTREE_PATH, KUNJ_BRANCH in its environment. Edit the config file by hand to list several commands as a JSON array. Executable scripts named pre-worktree-create in ~/.kunj/hooks or ~/.kunj/<repo>/hooks run as well; see `kunj hooks`.

settings.description: Command run by the post-worktree-create hook
settings.detailedDescription: Runs inside a freshly created worktree, after keep files have been copied in (e.g. to install dependencies). The command runs through the shell with ${repoRoot}, ${repoconfig}, ${repoName}, ${home}, ${worktree}, ${worktreePath}, ${branch} expanded, and receives KUNJ_HOOK, KUNJ_REPO_ROOT, KUNJ_WORKTREE_PATH, KUNJ_BRANCH in its environment. settings.description: Container image override (default: the repo's devcontainer, else kunj-sandbox)
Command `kunj container agent` runs inside the container (in tmux)
Host environment variable names forwarded into containers when set; NAME=value entries are passed literally

When container.env names GH_TOKEN and the host env has no GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN or GITLAB_TOKEN, forward `gh auth token` for origin's GitHub host as GH_TOKEN. The agent in the container can use this token with everything your gh login can do; false turns it off
Host files copied into new containers, as hostPath:containerPath
Copy the repository's keep files into new containers
Egress allowlist of domains; empty means open internet (the host and LAN are always blocked)
Allow containers to reach the Docker host (host.docker.internal)
Docker context used for every docker call
Run this repository's containers on a remote kunj serve (a name from kunj remote add); empty: the laptop's Docker
CPU limit passed to docker run (e.g. 2)
Memory limit passed to docker run (e.g. 4g)
Ports always published at container start
`kunj container agent` starts a background `forward --auto` that forwards every new port the container listens on to 127.0.0.1
Container ports `forward --auto` never forwards (ports below 1024 are never forwarded)
`kunj container prune` also removes stopped containers created more than this many days ago (0 = off)
settings.detailedDescription: Off by default. A container removed this way still has to pass the remove guard (no unpushed commits, stashes or uncommitted changes) unless prune is run with --force.

settings.description: Docker inside branch containers: off, sysbox (needs the sysbox-runc runtime on the Docker host) or privileged (needs container.allowPrivileged; refused on Docker Desktop)
settings.detailedDescription: Each container then runs its own dockerd, its /var/lib/docker on a per-branch volume, so docker compose up works inside. The container keeps its capabilities. sysbox keeps inner containers inside the sandbox's user namespace; privileged gives the container root on the Docker host (on a Mac, its VM), so use it only on a dedicated Docker context. Needs the kunj sandbox image (no devcontainer or container.image).

settings.description: Allow container.dockerInDocker "privileged" (root on the Docker host or its VM); it is still refused on Docker Desktop
Sidecar services (Postgres, Redis, ...) started next to each branch container, by name
settings.detailedDescription: An object of name: { image, env?, command?, port?, healthcheck?, volumes?, dependsOn? }; edit the config file by hand. Each service runs on the branch's own network and is reached by its name (postgres:5432). It gets only the env declared here, only named volumes (created per branch), no added capabilities and no published ports. The blueprint's services win over these by name, and these over the devcontainer's compose services.

settings.description: MCP servers on this machine bridged into the container for its Claude Code; only "chrome" (a browser) for now
settings.detailedDescription: An object of name: { command?, args?, env?, allowOrigins? }; edit the config file by hand (host config only, never the blueprint). Off while empty, because the agent then drives a browser on this machine and its network. {"chrome": {}} runs npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@1.12.0 (performance, memory and file: navigation off) with an empty profile per session that refuses downloads, in a temp directory deleted afterwards, when `kunj ct agent` starts, and adds a matching entry to the container user's ~/.claude.json. The server gets only PATH, HOME and its env. Only a fixed list of browser tools and arguments passes, so no file path from the agent reaches the server; with your own command or args there is no throwaway profile and downloads land where that browser puts them (normally ~/Downloads). navigate_page and new_page may open only the host ports forwarded for the container, unless allowOrigins lists origins (with a port: that port; without: any port, which is broad). This limits explicit navigation only: a click or a script can still take the page elsewhere. One session at a time per server.

settings.description: Command `kunj agent` runs in a host tmux session for a worktree
Command `kunj agent --agent antigravity` runs (the Antigravity CLI)
Run agents in a tmux session (kunj agent, kunj ct agent) so they outlive the terminal and can be reattached; false runs them directly, like --no-tmux
Show tmux's status line in agent sessions (off by default: the workspace app and the terminal show the session already)
Pass Claude Code hooks to the agent that report when it waits for input (agent.state in worktree list and ct list)
Where the secrets vault key comes from: auto (macOS Keychain, else libsecret, else a passphrase), keychain, libsecret or passphrase
settings.detailedDescription: Picks the key provider for a new vault. An existing vault keeps its kdf: a passphrase vault always asks for its passphrase, and KUNJ_SECRETS_KEY (64 hex chars) overrides the keychain for keychain vaults.

settings.description: Stop a language server that keeps a cache on disk (gopls, sourcekit-lsp, clangd) after this many idle minutes, even with tabs open
Stop a language server without a disk cache (typescript-language-server) after this many idle minutes, even with tabs open
Stop a language server this many minutes after the last editor tab of its language in that worktree closes
At most this many language servers run at once; starting another stops one (a cached one first, else the least recently used)
A go to definition waits this long for a starting server before it searches instead
Language servers by language, over the built-in ones (typescript, swift, go, cpp)
settings.detailedDescription: An object of language: { command, extensions?, restart?, cachePaths? }. An entry replaces the built-in server of that language or adds a new one; see `kunj lsp list`.
